trust_decision.summary: Admin metrics API decides who may trigger expensive date-range analytics queries and how wide the range may be; the retention controller runs the cohort query in a before_action before `authorize :dashboard, :index?` (auth is skipped entirely without a token), and none of retention/measures/dimensions bound start_at..end_at.

landing_point.why: Summary names the unauthenticated admin retention API; the before_action that eagerly calls `.cohorts` ahead of `authorize` is the obvious first stop.

fix_sites.module_kind: controller: before_action made lazy (cohorts computed after authorize) + params.require(:start_at/:end_at)
metrics library: range clamp to 31 days (day) / 12 months (month)
base class in metrics library: 2-year clamp shared by 14 measure subclasses
base class in metrics library: conditional 2-year clamp; its controller app/controllers/api/v1/admin/dimensions_controller.rb was NOT changed

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: app/lib/admin/metrics/dimension/base_dimension.rb:14-20 (and app/lib/admin/metrics/measure/base_measure.rb:14-19): range clamp lives in the shared base classes behind the measures/dimensions endpoints, not in the retention path the report names

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Measures and dimensions compute lazily at render time, after `authorize` (app/controllers/api/v1/admin/measures_controller.rb:11-13, app/lib/admin/metrics/measure.rb:24 only instantiates), so they are not reachable unauthenticated; a solver can argue they are admin-only and outside an 'unauthenticated retention' report.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Admin instance-impact report posts to /api/v1/admin/measures with start_at: null / end_at: null for instance_accounts/follows/followers measures whose totals are not time-ranged; also dashboard retention uses frequency 'month' over 6 months and dimensions with small limits. A fix that requires/rejects missing dates or clamps too tightly breaks these. Note: the published fix's params.require(:start_at) on measures appears to break this null-date call itself (unverified).

O6_input_shapes: missing start_at/end_at (nil) -> params.require now 400s instead of nil-safe &.to_date (fix.diff:46-48, fix.diff:79-80)
very wide range with frequency=day (clamped to 31 days, fix.diff:134)
very wide range with frequency=month or invalid frequency falling back to day (fix.diff:131-134)
wide range on any of 14 measure keys via keys[] array (fix.diff:114)
wide range on dimension keys only when both dates present (fix.diff:95)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Dimensions endpoint: user-supplied `limit` is passed unbounded (to_i) into the SQL LIMIT of every dimension query; the fix clamped only the date range.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Admin-only (computed after authorize), a row cap rather than an input-driven loop, and the dashboard always sends small limits (app/views/admin/dashboard/index.html.haml:72).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different controller and base class from the landing point (app/controllers/api/v1/admin/dimensions_controller.rb:23 -> app/lib/admin/metrics/dimension/*.rb)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Dimensions controller still reads params[:keys]/[:start_at]/[:end_at] without require and keeps them nil-tolerant, so the base_dimension clamp is skipped when either date is absent.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Several dimensions (instance_accounts, space_usage, software_versions) legitimately ignore dates, and nil dates do not widen the scanned range.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: sibling controller in the same directory

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a new admin/API caller passing a request-supplied start_at to ActivityTracker#get, which maps one Redis read per day
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ActivityTracker already backs active_users/interactions measures (app/lib/admin/metrics/measure/active_users_measure.rb:19) and a public instance-activity endpoint (app/controllers/api/v1/instances/activity_controller.rb:39-47); a maintainer exposing a configurable window would forward params naturally.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a tag-history measure that overrides time_period or builds its own range from params, bypassing the base_measure clamp
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Subclasses already call time_period.map per day; an override in one subclass is a plausible maintenance change and sits outside the base-class clamp (HOW-type).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a before_action that eagerly calls `.data`/`.map(&:data)` ahead of authorize, like the retention controller did
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Identical controller template to retention; copying the old retention pattern is realistic.

O9_family: uncontrolled resource consumption (unbounded date-range analytics queries, quadratic cohort cross join) combined with authorization evaluated after expensive work in a before_action

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby/Bundler, Rails, RSpec; Node/Yarn only for frontend assets

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Move `.cohorts` after `authorize` (or call doorkeeper_authorize! unconditionally) in the retention controller only, leaving every date range unbounded for retention, measures and dimensions.
